teaser.en: Its grain heads look like long, grey-green candles, and they survive where maize gives up.

summary.en: Pearl millet is a hardy cereal with long cylindrical grain heads. On the Digo coast it is a minor grain of the dry inland farms, ground for porridge and *ugali*.

about.en:
Pearl millet is a tall cereal grass with broad leaves and stems ending in a long, dense, cylindrical head packed with small, round, pearl-grey grains. The heads can be as long as a forearm.

It is one of the most drought-tolerant cereals in the world.

where.en: Pearl millet is a minor grain grown on dry inland farms, where rain is too uncertain for maize.

uses.en: The grain is ground into flour for porridge and *ugali*.

names.en: No Digo name has been recorded yet. The Mgombato dictionary glosses *mhama* as 'millet', but gives the Swahili *mtama*, which normally means sorghum, so it probably does not refer to this plant. Swahili: *mwele* or *uwele*. English: pearl millet. Scientists call it *Pennisetum glaucum* (now also *Cenchrus americanus*).

reason.en: Maize, the main cereal for ugali

sources: Mwalonya, Nicolle, Nicolle & Zimbu, Mgombato: Digo-English-Swahili Dictionary (BTL / Digo Language and Literacy Project, 2004; e-version 2005)
